text:
liam: Heads-up 1: sketching an API-level "routing_intent" to let callers indicate performance/consistency tradeoffs and desired fallback behaviour across hosted/dedicated/private. want feedback before i put an RFC follow-up.
nora: curious to see the exact fields. goal being minimal surface for callers, yeah?
liam: yes. current draft:```json
{
  "routing_intent": {
    "priority": "performance",   // performance | cost | reliability
    "fallback_strategy": "queue_then_fallback", // queue_then_fallback | immediate_fail | degrade_then_fallback
    "residency_constraint": "fixed", // fixed | flexible
    "slo_tag": "p99<300ms", // optional freeform label for downstream correlation
    "max_queue_ms": 200 // only when queue_then_fallback
  }
}
```
anika: I like the explicit "residency_constraint" instead of naming "private/dedicated". Important: fixed -> never route outside local jurisdiction. must be enforced by PolicyTranslator.
raj: queue_then_fallback feels risky for user-facing sync calls (can increase p99 a lot). maybe allow callers to pick queue windows or system picks based on client type.
liam: agreed. plan: SDKs default to immediate_fail for sync; queue_then_fallback only for async or when caller opts-in.
ops-bot: Note: INF-4220 created: "routing_intent V0 - policy translator + admission semantics" (owner: unassigned).
anika: telemetry: every decision needs labels: intent_priority, decision, reason_code, original_target. also emit an audit.trace with before/after route.
nora: question on billing: if we queue and then fallback to hosted, how do we tag tokens for billing? we need a reconciliation_id emitted with the request so ledger can attribute correctly.
raj: secret/KMS concern: if fallback lands on hosted with different KMS, that's a hard policy block for residency_constraint=fixed. i propose: runtime checks KMS compatibility and if incompatible, treat as immediate_fail regardless of fallback_strategy.
liam: good. adding compatibility check to PolicyTranslator. also: fallback_strategy degrade_then_fallback = route to a quantized/cheaper variant in the same estate, then only fallback across estates if allowed.
anika: edge-case: dedicated surge -> degrade_then_fallback could silently impact quality. need explicit audit + consumer-visible header indicating "model_variant" used.
ops-bot: Suggestion: add a short-lived request header "x-routing-warn" that SDK surfaces when a downgrade/fallback occurs.
nora: for control-plane vs caller-managed quotas: i prefer control-plane managed default. caller-managed is advanced and must be opt-in via account setting.
liam: noted. Also drafting a runtime mapping doc: priority->mapping
- performance -> nvlink-enabled pools, prewarm cache
- cost -> batched quantized instances, higher-latency packing
- reliability -> replicate across two pools, prefer dedicated+hosted hybrid
will attach to RFC follow-up.
raj: test plan: simulate capacity pressure on dedicated, verify decisions: immediate_fail vs queue_then_fallback vs degrade_then_fallback; check audit logs, billing tags, KMS compatibility; run alerting to ensure on-escalate incidents created.
anika: i'll own translation tests for residency + KMS. nora: i'll own SDK defaults and header surface. liam: i'll write RFC follow-up PR with schema + runtime mapping + test matrix.
liam: ok let's aim to lock wording Wed EOD. thanks all :thumbsup:
